_readme: Round 3 of 7 — big august 9th batch (in-copyright PDFs). Synopses grounded in real detect.mjs-extracted text; mentions curated from candidates.json per docs/detector.md exclusion rules; genres per tools/genres.mjs.

books.title: Good Night, Mr. Wodehouse
books.author: Faith Sullivan
books.synopsis: Set in the small Minnesota town of Harvester from the early 1900s through the 1940s, the novel follows Nell Stillman through marriage, widowhood, and raising her son Hilly, with the comic novels of P. G. Wodehouse serving as a recurring source of comfort and escape through her hardships.

books.title: Grimus
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.synopsis: Flapping Eagle, a Native American man granted immortality by a mysterious elixir, wanders the earth for centuries before following his equally immortal sister's trail to Calf Island, a fantastical, dimension-bending land ruled by the reclusive, godlike Grimus, whose power over reality and the island's inhabitants Flapping Eagle must ultimately confront.

books.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel: The Fates of Human Societies
books.author: Jared Diamond
books.synopsis: Diamond argues that the divergent historical trajectories of societies on different continents stem from geographic and environmental factors: the availability of domesticable plants and animals and continental axis orientation, which gave some regions a head start in food production leading to denser populations, epidemic diseases, writing, technology, and centralized political organization. The book traces this argument from the Cajamarca encounter between Pizarro and Atahuallpa through the origins of farming, livestock-borne germs, writing, and technology, then applies the framework to Polynesia, China, Eurasia, and Africa.

books.title: Homo Deus: A Brief History of Tomorrow
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.synopsis: Harari argues that having largely tamed famine, plague, and war, humankind's next projects will be pursuing immortality, bliss, and divine-like power, tracing how the humanist belief in individual free will and inner experience may be superseded by dataism, biotechnology, and artificial intelligence.

books.title: How to Get Filthy Rich in Rising Asia
books.author: Mohsin Hamid
books.synopsis: A satirical self-help book narrated in second person that tracks an unnamed protagonist's rise from rural poverty in an unnamed South Asian country to wealth through bottled water and real-estate ventures, tracing his moves to the city, his education, work, romance with 'the pretty girl,' entanglements with violence and bureaucracy, and eventual old age and death.

books.title: If Beale Street Could Talk
books.author: James Baldwin
books.synopsis: Nineteen-year-old Tish Rivers narrates her efforts, alongside her family, to prove the innocence of her fiance Fonny Hunt, jailed in New York on a rape charge he did not commit, while she carries their child.

books.title: In Cold Blood
books.author: Truman Capote
books.synopsis: A nonfiction account of the November 1959 murder of the Clutter family in Holcomb, Kansas, reconstructing the crime, the investigation, and the capture, trial, and execution of killers Perry Smith and Dick Hickock through interviews with townspeople, investigators, and the killers themselves.

books.title: Interface
books.author: Stephen Bury
books.synopsis: After a stroke, Illinois governor William Cozzano is secretly fitted with a brain implant that lets political operatives feed him poll-tested responses in real time as he runs a manipulated presidential campaign.

books.title: Into the War
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.synopsis: Three autobiographical narratives set in San Remo in 1940, following the teenage narrator and his fellow Avanguardisti through Italy's entry into the Second World War, a stint helping evacuees in occupied Menton, and nights spent on anti-aircraft duty.

books.title: Italo Calvino
books.author: Martin McLaughlin
books.synopsis: A critical study tracing Calvino's career book by book, from the early short stories and The Path to the Spiders' Nests through the Our Ancestors trilogy, the Cosmicomic stories, Invisible Cities, and If on a Winter's Night a Traveller, situating each work within its literary influences and intertexts.

books.title: Jazz
books.author: Toni Morrison
books.synopsis: In 1926 Harlem, cosmetics salesman Joe Trace shoots his young lover Dorcas after she leaves him for someone else, and at the girl's funeral his wife Violet slashes the corpse's face with a knife.

books.title: Jurassic Park
books.author: Michael Crichton
books.synopsis: Paleontologist Alan Grant and a small group of scientists are invited to inspect billionaire John Hammond's island resort, where dinosaurs have been cloned from ancient DNA, just before the park's security systems fail and the animals get loose.

books.title: Letting Go
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: Gabe Wallach, a young academic in 1950s Chicago and New York, becomes entangled in the troubled marriage of his friends Paul and Libby Herz while avoiding commitments of his own.

books.title: Literary Life: A Second Memoir
books.author: Larry McMurtry
books.synopsis: McMurtry recounts his development as a novelist and man of letters, from his early influences and the writing of his first books through decades of reading, teaching, and the movie adaptations of his fiction.

books.title: Moth Smoke
books.author: Mohsin Hamid
books.synopsis: After losing his bank job in Lahore, Daru Shezad slides into drug use, petty crime, and an affair with Mumtaz, the wife of his wealthy best friend Ozi.

books.title: Mother Mary Comes to Me
books.author: Arundhati Roy
books.synopsis: Arundhati Roy's memoir traces her fraught, intense bond with her mother Mary Roy, a strong-willed school founder in Kerala, from a chaotic childhood in Ayemenem and Kottayam through Roy's own path into architecture, screenwriting, activism, and the writing of The God of Small Things and The Ministry of Utmost Happiness. The book closes with Roy reflecting on her mother's death and imagining her still walking the shoreline of memory.

books.title: Mr Palomar
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.synopsis: A middle-aged man named Mr Palomar attempts to observe the world with total precision, fixing his attention in turn on a single wave, a gecko catching insects, a flock of starlings over Rome, a cheese shop, a zoo, and the ruins of Tula, each observation spiraling into meditation on knowledge, meaning, and his own place in things. The book closes with Palomar setting out to describe every instant of his life so as to postpone death, and dying in that same moment.

books.title: Murder on the Orient Express
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.synopsis: When the Orient Express is stalled by snow in the Balkans, wealthy American passenger Ratchett is found stabbed to death in his locked compartment, and detective Hercule Poirot, who is aboard the same train, questions the twelve other passengers in the coach to determine who among them killed him.

books.title: My Name Is Red
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.synopsis: In 16th-century Istanbul, miniaturist and illuminator Enishte Effendi is commissioned to secretly illustrate a book for the Sultan in the Frankish style, and when one of the workshop's master miniaturists is found murdered, the narration passes between multiple voices — including the corpse, the murderer, Enishte's daughter Shekure, her suitor Black, and the miniaturists Master Osman, Butterfly, Stork, and Olive — as they piece together who among the illustrators is the killer.

books.title: Nemesis
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: Set in Newark in the summer of 1944, the novel follows playground director Bucky Cantor as a polio epidemic spreads through his Jewish neighborhood, forcing him to weigh his duty to the children under his care against an offer to join his fiancée Marcia at a Pocono Mountains summer camp, Indian Hill. The narrative moves between the fear and death on the Chancellor Avenue playground and camp life at Indian Hill, including Indian Night ceremonies and a climactic javelin-throwing scene.

books.title: Nights of Plague
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.synopsis: Presented as a historian's edition of Princess Pakize's letters, the novel follows the Ottoman-era plague outbreak of 1901 on the fictional Mediterranean island of Mingheria, where Doctor Nuri and Princess Pakize navigate quarantine measures, the murder of the Sultan's Royal Chemist Bonkowski Pasha, and the political unraveling that leads to Mingheria's revolution and declared independence under Commander Kâmil.

books.title: On James Baldwin
books.author: Colm Tóibín
books.synopsis: Colm Tóibín weaves his own history of reading James Baldwin, beginning with Go Tell It on the Mountain at eighteen, into a critical and biographical account of Baldwin's fiction, essays, and public life — his novels, his years in Paris and Harlem, his friendships and rivalries with writers like Richard Wright and Norman Mailer, and his civil-rights-era encounters with figures such as Robert Kennedy and Malcolm X.

books.title: On Literature
books.author: Umberto Eco
books.synopsis: A collection of Eco's occasional essays and lectures on literature, ranging from Dante's Paradiso and Aristotle's Poetics to his own novels, tracing the social functions of literature, the practice of intertextual irony, and his personal debts to writers like Borges.

books.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
books.author: Ken Kesey
books.synopsis: Narrated by Chief Bromden, a large half-Indian patient who feigns deafness and muteness on a psychiatric ward run by the controlling Big Nurse (Ratched), the novel follows Randle McMurphy, a brash new patient who challenges her authority through card games, a deep-sea fishing trip, and a late-night party, provoking escalating retaliation including electroshock and lobotomy.

books.title: Our Gang
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: A satirical send-up of a Nixon-like president called Tricky Dixon, told through interviews, press conferences, and dialogue: he defends his stance on 'sanctity of human life' while dodging on Vietnam and Cambodia, gets ambushed by advisers deciding whom to blame for domestic unrest, is implicated in the disappearance of baseball player Curt Flood, and is eventually assassinated and sent to Hell, where he runs for office against Satan.
